properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. O-20 of the hxm_program hub's 2026-09-28 report (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28).

THE REPORTER'S WORDS: "An operations mode for gap weighting. When a project declares it is in operations (`set_project_mode` already exists), rank open incidents, failing or stale checks, and safety-tagged findings above design-completeness gaps, and batch the latter into a periodic review instead of every orientation. Add a `safety` tag on findings that always surfaces first."

WHAT IS MEASURED ALREADY (fact:root-cause-the-loops-order-is-fixed-for-the-design-phase-and-the-operations-signal-is-not-in-it-2026-09-28):
· `next` is a fixed sequence in code.
· set_project_mode carries governance only ([flexible, rigid], the apply_heal gate) and refuses "operations"; no Project property records a phase.
· Open defect findings and failing checks are never lines of `next`.
· A finding has no safety field. `concern: safety` exists only on Requirement and Constraint.
· Gaps can be quieted only one reason at a time, by design.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A DECLARED LIFECYCLE PHASE on the Project (for example concept, design, build, operations), kept apart from governance mode. The loop reads it: operations puts incidents, failing or stale checks and safety first, and holds design-completeness gaps for a periodic review. Medium: a schema property, a reorder in the loop, and the skills that read it.
(b) NO PHASE, AN URGENCY MARK. A `safety` (or urgency) value on a finding that always leads `next`, whatever the project is doing. Small to medium: a field, one loop line, and a reader for open findings the loop lacks today.
(c) A RULING THAT PARKS A KIND OF GAP. The owner says once, visibly and revisably, that a class of question ("which drawing standard") does not apply to this project, instead of 43 per-gap reasons that expire as the design moves. Medium, and it touches dec:bulk-keeps-the-judgement-per-item.
(d) A SESSION VIEW: a snooze, or "only what changed since my last call" (this hub's F-14, 2026-09-10). This answers the repetition without any phase. Medium.
(e) NOTHING NEW: acknowledge and withdraw by hand.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· This road was weighed once. dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing (accepted 2026-08-19) chose "detecting is not asking" over "a user-set posture, a computed phase, and full lifecycle phases — all of which ask the user to declare something". Option (a) reopens that for a different complaint (ranking rather than interruption), and a declared phase goes stale: this hub does design work and operations in the same week.
· A safety mark in a design tool can read as a safety system. At a facility, "safety" names formal procedures, and a record in reflow2 is not an interlock or a hazard review. The mark must never be read as assurance. And a tag nobody sets, or everybody sets, carries no signal.
· Batching gaps into a "periodic review" can hide them for good. The loop's purpose is that nothing is forgotten, and req:detecting-is-not-asking already separates detection from invitation.
· Fewer things well: (b), (c) and (d) serve every project, not only operating ones. (a) is operations-specific and belongs to the umbrella question.
· FOR it: a safety concern with no way to outrank "which quality attribute is this for" is the loop failing at its one job, which is saying what matters now. And the loop already reads a Project property (mode) to change what apply_heal does, so a project-level switch changing loop behaviour has a precedent.

2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY: the question this idea depends on is settled. Anthony: reflow2 serves a design for its whole life, concept → operations, and the loop runs as long as the system lives (dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design, accepted). The dependency is met. What stays open here is HOW the loop ranks an operating project's signal; the counter-arguments above weigh the how, never whether operations belongs in reflow2. Where this text or its DEPENDS_ON evidence speaks of the umbrella's options, those options are withdrawn: the question was never open (fact:root-cause-the-lifecycle-scope-lives-in-the-vision-and-the-graph-holds-one-line-so-a-brainstorm-reopened-it-2026-09-28). The 2026-08-19 ruling against asking users to declare a phase (dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing) still stands and still bears on option (a) here.

2026-09-28, A FURTHER OPTION, from Anthony's point the same day that epochs and increments exist because "many designs continue development and operations simultaneously" (req:epochs-can-be-planned):
(f) DERIVE IT, DON'T DECLARE IT. A design has something in operations when an increment or release of it is deployed (DEPLOYED_TO an Environment, or a fielded increment). The loop could read that and rank the operating increment's signal first: its incidents, and its failing or stale checks. Meanwhile design-completeness gaps stay attached to the increments still in development. This needs no project-wide phase, so it does not reopen the 2026-08-19 ruling against asking users to declare one. It also fits a project doing design work and operations in the same week, because both are true at once. Counter-argument: many projects, this hub included, never record releases or deployments, so the signal would be absent where it is most needed, unless adopting a running system records its current state as a deployed increment.
properties.name: OPEN — when a project is in operations, should the loop rank open incidents, failing or stale checks and safety-marked findings above design-completeness gaps, batch those gaps into a periodic review, and let a safety mark always surface first?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill (fetched fresh) during the triage of art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28. Searched first (operations mode, gap weighting, safety tag, lifecycle phase, periodic review): the nearest are the accepted 2026-08-19 ruling that weighed and declined declared phases, the session-owes requirement, and the severity-blind count finding from this hub's earlier report. The root-cause walk of F-33 is recorded separately, and this is the report's idea for it.
